issues.t: Won't start with the security light flashing (Passlock)
issues.sym: The engine cranks but never fires, or starts and dies right away. The security or anti-theft light on the dash stays on or flashes. It often comes and goes.
issues.why: The Passlock anti-theft system uses a sensor in the ignition lock area. When that sensor, the lock cylinder or its wiring wears out, the system thinks the car is being stolen and cuts fuel to the engine. This is the most-reported Alero problem.
issues.next: Try the owner workaround: turn the key to On (engine off) and leave it about 10 minutes until the security light stops flashing, switch off for 10 to 30 seconds, then start. If it keeps happening, have a shop test the Passlock sensor and lock cylinder rather than replacing parts at random.

issues.t: Cranks but won't start or dies from a failing fuel pump
issues.sym: The engine turns over but won't catch, starts only some of the time, sputters, or shuts off while driving, with no security light involved.
issues.why: The electric fuel pump inside the tank wears out, often somewhere between 30,000 and 135,000 miles. A clogged fuel filter makes the pump work harder and can speed this up.
issues.next: Have the fuel pressure tested before buying parts, since Passlock faults look similar. If pressure is low, replace the pump and the fuel filter together.

issues.t: Intake manifold gasket coolant leak
issues.sym: You keep adding coolant, see a puddle or sweet smell, the temperature gauge climbs, or the low coolant light comes on. In bad cases the oil turns milky.
issues.why: The factory intake manifold gaskets on the 3.4L V6 break down over time and let coolant leak out, or into the oil. Many owners also blame the Dex-Cool coolant. Most failures show up around 90,000 miles.
issues.next: Don't keep driving it low on coolant; overheating can ruin the engine, and coolant in the oil wipes out the bearings. Have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and replace the upper and lower gaskets with the updated design.

issues.t: Automatic transmission shifts hard or fails
issues.sym: Jerky or hard shifts, engine revs jumping between gears, a check engine light, or the transmission losing gears one by one.
issues.why: Some cases trace back to simple sensors (air temperature or throttle position) feeding the computer bad data. Others are a failed shift solenoid or internal wear that needs a rebuild, usually past 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the trouble codes read first; a sensor fix is far simpler than a rebuild. If a solenoid or internal failure is found, get a second opinion from an independent transmission shop.

issues.t: Turn signals work only sometimes or keep clicking
issues.sym: The turn signals or hazards stop working, work only half the time, or the flasher keeps clicking after you shut the car off.
issues.why: The turn signal (multifunction) switch on the steering column wears out and makes poor contact. Over 150 owners have reported it on RepairPal.
issues.next: Get it fixed soon, since other drivers can't see your turns. A shop can confirm the switch is at fault and replace it.

issues.t: Turn signals can stop working from the hazard switch (recall)
issues.sym: The turn signals stop working, so you can't signal turns or lane changes.
issues.why: A faulty hazard warning switch can cut power to the turn signals. GM recalled these cars (NHTSA 03V327) to replace it.
issues.next: Ask an Oldsmobile/GM dealer to check your VIN for open recall work. Use hand signals until it's repaired.

issues.t: Horn blows by itself
issues.sym: The horn goes off on its own, sometimes overnight or in cold weather, and keeps blaring until you pull the horn fuse or the fuse blows.
issues.why: The horn contacts are built into the steering wheel airbag cover. As that cover ages and shrinks, it can press on the horn switch.
issues.next: Pull the horn fuse to stop it in the meantime. A lasting fix means replacing the horn contacts or the airbag/horn pad; have this done by a shop since it involves the airbag.

issues.t: Dashboard cover wrinkles, shrinks or peels
issues.sym: The top of the dash wrinkles, bubbles or pulls away, especially above the glove box and around the airbag door.
issues.why: The vinyl dash cover breaks down with heat and sun, though some garage-kept cars are affected too.
issues.next: This is mostly cosmetic, but check that nothing is lifting near the passenger airbag door. A dash cap or cover is a simpler option than replacing the whole dash panel.

issues.t: Power window falls into the door or stops working
issues.sym: A window won't go up or down, slides down on its own, or you hear grinding or a snap from inside the door.
issues.why: The window regulator uses plastic pulleys and clips that crack and break with age.
issues.next: Tape or wedge the glass up if it won't stay closed. Replace the regulator (often sold with the motor) for that door.

issues.t: Key won't turn or sticks in the ignition
issues.sym: The key won't turn in the ignition, gets stuck and won't come out, or the lock binds, sometimes with the security light on.
issues.why: The ignition lock cylinder wears out. Because the Passlock sensor is tied to the lock cylinder, a worn cylinder often brings security-light problems with it.
issues.next: Don't force the key; a broken key makes the job harder. Have the lock cylinder replaced and the Passlock system relearned.

issues.t: Ignition switch can slip out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can shut off while driving if the key is bumped or the key ring is heavy, and you lose power steering and power brakes.
issues.why: The ignition switch can move out of the Run position. If that happens, the airbags may not deploy in a crash. This is part of GM's large 2014 ignition switch recall (NHTSA 14V400).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have a GM dealer check your VIN for open recall work. Until then, carry only the ignition key with nothing heavy hanging from it.

issues.t: Engine stalls or dies while driving
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving or at stops, or starts but won't stay running. It may restart after sitting.
issues.why: Owners trace it to several causes, including a failing fuel pump, the Passlock system, sensors or the ignition module. There is no single fix.
issues.next: Pull over safely and have the codes read right after it happens. Tell the shop whether the security light was on, since that points to Passlock rather than fuel or ignition.

issues.t: Gauges read wrong or stop working
issues.sym: The fuel gauge jumps around, the temperature gauge stops moving, or the dash lights and gauges act up.
issues.why: The instrument cluster or its circuit boards develop faults with age. Owners report erratic fuel gauges, dead coolant gauges and full cluster failures.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Don't trust a dead gauge: watch your mileage between fill-ups and keep an eye out for overheating. A cluster repair or rebuild shop can usually fix the unit.

issues.t: Blower fan works only on some speeds
issues.sym: The heater/A-C fan works only on high, or some fan speeds are missing.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor, which sets the lower fan speeds, burns out.
issues.next: Replace the blower motor resistor. If it fails again quickly, have the blower motor checked, since a worn motor can overload the resistor.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle or failure
issues.sym: Rattling from the engine, misfires, rough idle, a check engine light, or a no-start. Metal flakes may show up in the oil.
issues.why: On early 2.2L Ecotec engines the timing chain tensioner gets too little oil at idle and wears out. Low oil makes it worse.
issues.next: Keep the oil full and changed on time. If you hear a rattle, have the chain and tensioner checked before the chain jumps or breaks.

issues.t: Warped front rotors and sticking calipers
issues.sym: The steering wheel or pedal shakes when braking, a grinding noise, or a car that pulls to one side because a caliper sticks.
issues.why: Brakes are one of the most-reported complaint areas for these years. Owners report warped rotors, stuck calipers and ABS-related faults.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected. Replace pads and rotors as a set per axle, and replace any caliper that doesn't release.

issues.t: Center console lid may open in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom while driving.
issues.why: In a crash the console cover could open, and the lid or items stored in it could hit someone. GM recalled these cars (NHTSA 00V140).
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for open recall work. Keep heavy items out of the console until then.

issues.t: Steering wheel may come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The steering wheel may feel loose or shift on the column.
issues.why: A defect with the steering wheel attachment could lead to loss of steering control. GM recalled these cars (NHTSA 98V320).
issues.next: If the wheel feels loose at all, don't drive the car. Have a dealer check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Key can come out when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: You can pull the key out while the shifter is still in a driving gear.
issues.why: The shift interlock didn't work as federal rules require, so the car could be left in gear and roll. GM recalled some cars (NHTSA 00V372).
issues.next: Always confirm the car is in Park and set the parking brake. Have a dealer check your VIN for open recall work.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal may not return to idle (recall)
issues.sym: The engine keeps revving after you lift off the gas pedal, or the pedal is slow to come back up.
issues.why: The accelerator pedal arm may not return to idle. GM recalled about 93,000 vehicles including the 2003 Alero (NHTSA 04V528).
issues.next: If the pedal sticks, shift to Neutral, brake to a stop and turn off the engine. Have a dealer check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Slow coolant leak or water pump leak
issues.sym: Coolant level drops over time, drips under the front of the engine, or the engine runs hot.
issues.why: Owners report leaking water pumps and slow leaks from hoses and the radiator on early cars.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested to find the leak, and fix it before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Engine won't turn over at all
issues.sym: Turning the key gives a click or nothing at all; the engine doesn't crank.
issues.why: Owners trace these to the battery, starter, ignition switch or alternator, and sometimes to Passlock. It is one of the most common electrical complaints for 2003-2004.
issues.next: Test the battery and charging system first, as that is the simplest fix. If the battery is good, have the starter and ignition switch checked.
